title: Mexico’s internet access is expanding and rural gaps are narrowing, but device, age, and territorial inequalities remain
source_unit: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Geografía (INEGI), ENDUTIH 2025
geography: Mexico; people aged 6 and over and private households, with national, urban-rural, state, age, and Indigenous self-identification dimensions

observations.period: 2025; Internet, household, mobile, and computer/tablet access

denominator.unit: sampled dwellings in the 2025 ENDUTIH; published percentages cover people aged 6+ or households as specified

internet_users.unit: percent of people aged 6 and over using the Internet

urban_internet_use.unit: percent of people aged 6+ in urban areas using the Internet

rural_internet_use.unit: percent of people aged 6+ in rural areas using the Internet

urban_rural_internet_gap.unit: percentage-point difference between urban and rural Internet use in 2025

households_with_internet.unit: percent of households with Internet access

mobile_phone_use.unit: percent of people aged 6+ using a mobile phone

computer_or_tablet_use.unit: percent of people aged 6+ using a computer, laptop, or tablet

mobile_computer_gap.unit: percentage-point difference between mobile-phone and computer/tablet use

mechanism.value: Mexico is moving toward broad Internet access and a narrower rural gap, but connectivity remains strongly mobile-first and does not imply equal access to computer-dependent tasks, services, or forms of digital production

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from INEGI ENDUTIH 2025 press release and results report; urban-rural and device gaps are calculated from published percentages.
observations.uncertainty: The survey measures availability/use indicators rather than speed, reliability, affordability, digital skills, task type, or outcomes; rural-gap comparisons across years reflect the survey's revised population estimates and design.
observations.subgroup: People aged 6 and over and households in Mexico, by urban-rural domain.
observations.counterinterpretation: Mobile-first access can be an efficient consumer choice rather than a deficit, and narrowing rural Internet gaps may coexist with persistent quality, device, language, affordability, or service-use differences.

observations.period: 2025; age, Indigenous self-identification, and state variation in Internet use

denominator.unit: sampled dwellings in the 2025 ENDUTIH; subgroup percentages are survey-weighted estimates for people aged 6+

internet_use_age_15_24.unit: percent of people aged 15-24 using the Internet

internet_use_age_75_plus.unit: percent of people aged 75 and over using the Internet

internet_use_age_75_plus_2015.unit: percent of people aged 75+ using the Internet in 2015

internet_users_indigenous_self_descripti.unit: percent of Internet users self-describing as Indigenous

household_internet_state_high.unit: percent of households with Internet in Mexico City, the highest state-level estimate

household_internet_state_low.unit: percent of households with Internet in Chiapas, the lowest state-level estimate

state_household_internet_gap.unit: percentage-point difference between highest and lowest named state-level household estimates

mechanism.value: Aggregate digital expansion can coexist with a very large life-stage and territorial divide: older adults are entering the Internet rapidly but remain far below youth, and state-level household access differs by more than thirty points

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from INEGI ENDUTIH 2025 results report and press release; age and state gaps are calculated from published subgroup percentages.
observations.uncertainty: Indigenous self-description among Internet users is not an Internet-use rate for Indigenous people and should not be interpreted as a group access comparison; state estimates reflect household composition, infrastructure, income, geography, and survey sampling.
observations.subgroup: Mexican people aged 6+, age groups, Internet users' self-description, and households by federal entity.
observations.counterinterpretation: The age gap may shrink through cohort replacement and continued adoption; state variation may capture urbanization and household resources rather than state policy or cultural preference alone.

related_sources.claim: Official INEGI six-page press release with headline Internet, urban-rural, household, mobile, computer/tablet, and survey-design measures.
Official INEGI 23-page ENDUTIH 2025 results report with age series, state tables, Indigenous variables, and methodological notes.
INEGI ENDUTIH program page describing scope, annual design, domains, sample, questionnaire, and documentation.

boundary: This record adds a Mexican digital-access, device, age, minority-identification, and state-variation layer. It does not establish digital skills, online consumer behavior, service quality, affordability, causal rural or state effects, or Indigenous group access rates.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: INEGI ENDUTIH program page, press release, and 23-page results report reviewed; 2025 national, urban-rural, historical, age, Indigenous self-description, state, device, sample, and revised-population notes checked.
